scope: R136 preregistered targeted confirmation on the physical router

rules.paired: Same window and lane; eight non-reused subject/control pairs.
rules.metric: Win: paired percentage median < -1% and >= 7/8 lower; loss: median > +1% and >= 7/8 higher; otherwise tie.
rules.primary: Candidate/R134 event_8 mean: paired percentage median < -1% and >= 7/8 lower.
rules.acceptance: Primary must pass and no mean/p95/p99 descriptive loss versus R134 in any of the five lanes; CPU savings cannot offset latency loss.

limitations: Every planned lane and metric is reported, including all candidate higher medians. Acceptance applies only these frozen targeted rules and does not imply global superiority or completed integration.
R135 and Oracle data are excluded from the eight R136 router pairs. No extra windows or data-dependent removal is allowed.
These are frozen engineering decision rules, not familywise-adjusted significance or equivalence tests. Each lane shares a daemon with the other lanes within a subject/window.
Process CPU clocks bracket the measurement interval; daemon CPU is distinct from caller CPU. Latencies are recomputed from all 10000 raw operation samples.
Events here are generated by object ADD/REMOVE, not general user SEND. This confirmation does not cover other ubusd lanes, resident memory or nine-component integration.
Archive and expanded evidence hashes agree. Driver assertions establish cleanup and unchanged production configuration/mounts; the report contains no raw device identity or process identifiers.

caller_erratum.actual_caller: The frozen owrt-benchmark uses Rust owrt_ubus::Connection for register-cycle/register-watch. C, R134, and candidate used the same benchmark ELF.
caller_erratum.impact: The workload/binary identity and frozen thresholds are unchanged. This is not an original libubus performance comparison.
